title: Conquest of Damascus by Ashur-Nirari III, Shoshenq I and Jeroboam II
summary: CFAH synchronises a conquest of Damascus by the Assyrian Ashur-Nirari III, the Egyptian Shoshenq I and Jeroboam II of Israel.
description: CFAH synchronises a conquest of Damascus by the Assyrian Ashur-Nirari III, the Egyptian Shoshenq I and Jeroboam II of Israel. Recorded from a CFAH OSF preprint anchor point (not yet published in ARJ). Added by the CFAH pass.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 1: CFAH anchor point: 806 BC (AP-77, OSF preprint CFAH-10)

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "CFAH-10: The Libyan-Cushite Intermediate Period," OSF preprint v1.4 (26 Dec 2025), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/FG4DV, file CFAH-10 The Libyan-Cushite Intermediate Period_v1.4.pdf, p. 12 ("Anchor Point 77, the Conquest of Damascus by Ashur-Nirari III, Shoshenq I, and Jeroboam II in 806 BC")

Griffith & White, "A Reply to Beckman’s Defense of Thiele’s Chronology, Part 2: An Objectivist Answer to the Assyrian Synchronisms," OSF preprint v2.10 (2025), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/DT6GX, section “The Tell al-Rimah Stela”, p. 14; Table 1, rows 806, pp. 37–38
chronologies.note: Adad-Nirari III’s fifth-year campaign against Damascus and Arpad (Eponym Chronicle and Tell al-Rimah Stela). Names “Mari of Damascus”, successor of Ben-Hadad son of Hazael, and a tribute claim from “Ia-a-su of Samaria”, read as an anachronism or a crown prince Jehoash.
